sections.heading: 1. Key Expressions & Sentences Reviewed (Lessons 141–147)
points: Lesson 141: "Mvura yanaya nhasi, saka tinofanira kunonoka kuenda kumunda." — It has rained today, so we should delay going to the field.
Lesson 142: "Muviri wangu unonzwa kuremerwa saka ndiri kuda kuzorora nhasi." — My body feels tired and heavy, so I want to rest today.
Lesson 143: "Nhasi zuva ririnani zvaro; asi mhepo iri kufefetera zvakasimba." — Today the weather is fairly pleasant, though a strong breeze is blowing.
Lesson 144: "Mungandibatsirawo here kusimudza bhokisi ririkurema iri?" — Could you please help me lift this heavy box?
Lesson 145: "Rwizi rweZambezi rwuripamuganhu peZimbabwe neZambia" — The Zambezi River lies on the border between Zimbabwe and Zambia.
Lesson 146: "Ndinokumbira kuti utore magwaro ose ari patafura, uwaise mufaira riri pamubhedha." — Please take all the documents on the table and put them in the file on the bed.
Lesson 147: "Mugwagwa wangauine makomba asi rwendo rwazofamba zvakanaka; pasina dambudziko." — The road had potholes, but the journey went well without any problem.

sections.heading: 2. Core Shona Grammar Rules Consolidated
points: Talking About the Past ('yanaya'): Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb
Actions Happening Right Now: The '-ri ku-' Progressive: [Subject + -ri] + ku-[verb] -> Ndiri kuverenga (I am reading) | Vari kufamba (They are walking) | Mvura iri kunaya (It is raining)
Talking About the Past ('zvakasimba'): Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb
Joining Words with 'ne-' ('and / with') in 'neZambia': ne- + Noun = and / with [Noun] (written as a single word, e.g., sadza nemuriwo = sadza and vegetables)
Present Tense & Everyday Actions ('Ndinokumbira'): [ndi- (I) / u- (you) / a- (he/she) / ti- (we) / va- (they)] + -no- + verb -> Ndinoda (I want), Vanogara (They live)
Talking About the Past ('zvakanaka'): Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb

sections.heading: 3. Cultural Context & Practical Usage
points: Working with Heavy Clay Soils ('Ivhu Rinomira Mvura') After Rain: When heavy rain falls at dawn ('mvura yanaya nhasi'), farmers wait a little before entering the field ('kunonoka kuenda kumunda') so the wet topsoil drains slightly and does not cling heavily to hoes and boots..

Listening to the Body ('Muviri Unonzwa Kuremerwa') & Rest: In Shona, physical fatigue is vividly described as the body 'feeling weighed down' ('muviri unonzwa kuremerwa'), a signal to take a day of rest and recovery at home..

Mild Highveld Days & Refreshing Breezes ('Kufefetera'): Notice the expressive verb '-fefetera'—used specifically for a steady, cooling breeze blowing across the landscape on a pleasant, mild day ('zuva riri nani zvaro')..

Using Potential Mood ('Mungandibatsirawo Here?') for Ultra-Polite Requests: Combining the respectful plural 'mu-', the potential marker '-nga-' ('could/would'), the object '-ndi-' ('me'), and '-wo' ('please') in 'Mungandibatsirawo here?' is the gold standard of polite Shona when asking someone to help lift a heavy box..

review_exercises.prompt: Unit 21 Review — Grammar Mastery: How do you say 'Although it rained heavily, we arrived home safely'?
options: Kana mvura ikanaya mangwana, hatisi kuenda kumunda.
Mvura iri kunaya kunze saka vana vari mumba.
Zuva rakabuda masikati mbatya dzikaoma nekukurumidza.
Kunyangwe mvura yakanaya zvakanyanya, takasvika kumba zvakanaka.
review_exercises.correct_answer: Kunyangwe mvura yakanaya zvakanyanya, takasvika kumba zvakanaka.
review_exercises.explanation: 'Kunyangwe' means 'although / even though', 'yakanaya' is past tense ('rained'), and 'takasvika' is 'we arrived'.

review_exercises.prompt: Unit 21 Review — Numbers & Colours: Which phrase means 'three white trucks and two black cars'?
options: marori machena matatu nemotokari nhema mbiri
rori chena imwe nemotokari tsvuku nhatu
makombi maviri chena nemabhazi mana matema
shangu nhema mbiri nehembe tsvuku imwe
review_exercises.correct_answer: marori machena matatu nemotokari nhema mbiri
review_exercises.explanation: 'Marori machena matatu' = 'three white trucks' and 'nemotokari nhema mbiri' = 'and two black cars'.

review_exercises.prompt: Unit 21 Review — Locatives & Existence: Which word means 'Inside the wooden bowl there are roasted caterpillars'?
options: Patafura pane mabhuku nezvinyoreso.
Mundiro yemuti mune madora akakangwa.
Kumusika kune michero nemiriwo mizhinji.
Parutivi pemugwagwa pane miti mirefu.
review_exercises.explanation: 'Mu-' ('inside') + 'ndiro yemuti' ('wooden bowl') pairs with 'mune' ('there is inside').

review_exercises.prompt: Unit 21 Review — Conditionals & Reciprocal Verbs: What does 'tikashanda nesimba tichibatsirana' mean?
options: when they finished working at the market
because he worked alone in the field
if we work hard helping one another
before you start writing the examination
review_exercises.correct_answer: if we work hard helping one another
review_exercises.explanation: 'Tikashanda nesimba' = 'if we work with strength/hard', and 'tichibatsirana' ('-an-' reciprocal suffix) = 'helping each other'.

review_exercises.prompt: Unit 21 Review — Cultural & Historical Vocabulary: What does the phrase 'zvivakwa zvematombo' refer to?
options: wooden handles used on farm hoes and shovels
modern traffic lights at city intersections
plastic tanks mounted beside houses to store water
stone structures / buildings of stone (the origin of the name Zimbabwe)
review_exercises.correct_answer: stone structures / buildings of stone (the origin of the name Zimbabwe)

review_exercises.prompt: Unit 21 Review — Translate this new synthesis sentence into English: 'Vanhu vazhinji vari kutengesa michero nemiriwo pamusika.'
options: Many people are selling fruits and vegetables at the market.
Our ancestors built stone walls without mortar long ago.
Two women are sitting under an umbrella near the road.
We are planning to visit our grandparents next month.
review_exercises.correct_answer: Many people are selling fruits and vegetables at the market.
review_exercises.explanation: 'Vanhu vazhinji' = 'Many people', 'vari kutengesa' = 'are selling', 'michero nemiriwo' = 'fruits and vegetables', 'pamusika' = 'at the market'.
